why: Nothing in the archive has run on a real 486 or any other physical PC, and no real VGA or VBE card, 8042 controller, keyboard, mouse or monitor has been used. Every boot and every program ran in QEMU (`-cpu 486`), headless DOSBox Staging or a browser.

Spike G's pull request is {{coming.g.pr}} ({{coming.g.state}}); its results are not in this archive yet, so neither emulator counts as verified here. Until a chapter is written, only QEMU has booted the native image as far as this archive can say.

VBE was asked for on QEMU's standard, Cirrus and VMware cards, and on the S3 model of DOSBox Staging and of js-dos. On Cirrus a VBE mode could not be left again without the BIOS and the text screen came back garbled (PR #14). A real card, a banked-only BIOS and a VBE 1.2 BIOS are untried, and a way to leave VBE on any card is the job of spike n3 ({{coming.n3.pr}}), which this archive has not read.
Only QEMU's SeaBIOS and a floppy image were tried here. IDE and hard-disk boot were not (PR #6).

what: Other DPMI hosts and memory managers.
why: Only CWSDPMI under DOSBox's own DOS (and, in the browser, inside js-dos). EMM386, QEMM, HDPMI and a Windows 9x DOS box were not tried (PRs #3, #4, #7, #11 and #15).

The keyboard and mouse drivers met QEMU's PS/2 model, DOSBox's keyboard and its built-in mouse driver. A USB-legacy 8042, a laptop touchpad, a wheel mouse, a lost byte on a real cable, key repeat and a real INT 33h driver are untried (PRs #10 and #15). The mouse wheel was tested on the host only on the native side.

js-dos ran in headless Chromium 154 on Linux. Firefox, Safari, other operating systems, touch and phones, and anything audible were not tried (PR #13). This archive's own pages were looked at in one browser as well.
The generator was tested by serving the files locally. Publishing needs the owner's sign-in, so the live page's controls have not been clicked by the author.

what: `std` on other Rust releases, and on hardware.
why: The patch to `std` was applied only on the pinned release; on older releases it applied partly, and whether the new files compile there was not tried (PR #12). Its clock was never run across midnight, and nothing ran on real hardware.
The fonts follow the era's TrueType rules, but Windows 3.1, 95, NT and OS/2 were not run. Neither were GDI, DirectWrite, macOS, Safari or Firefox (PR #1).

what: The fonts on a DOS screen.
why: The `.DFN` and `.DEM` files were checked against FreeType and a decoder in the tests; no DOS program has drawn them yet.
Audio cannot be checked headless. The js-dos spike measured the pitch of three tones from the emulator's sample stream, and nobody listened (PR #13).
CWSDPMI aborts the whole program before any signal handler runs, so it is not recoverable (PR #4). A null write was recovered only under QEMU with FreeDOS (by hand, not in CI).
Every rate and size in the graphics and `std` chapters was measured under an emulator on a fast machine. They show relative costs, not what a 486 does.
